:::{#exm-ldpc-code}
#### A $(2, 3)$-regular code of length 6

<!-- no-figure: the example is a small matrix and a count -->

Label the four vertices of a complete graph $1, 2, 3, 4$.
It has six edges, one for each pair of vertices.
Let $H$ have a row for each vertex and a column for each edge,
with a 1 where the vertex lies on the edge.
Every edge has two vertices and every vertex lies on three edges,
so $H$ has two ones in each column and three in each row,
and it gives a $(2, 3)$-regular code of length 6.
The R chunk below builds $H$, checks the counts,
and counts the words $y$ with $H y = 0$ modulo 2.

```{r}
#| label: ldpc-code
edges <- t(combn(4, 2))
H <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(edges)), function(e) as.integer(1:4 %in% edges[e, ]))
H
colSums(H)
rowSums(H)
words <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(0:1), 6)))
is_codeword <- apply(words, 1, function(y) all((H %*% y) %% 2 == 0))
sum(is_codeword)
```

The code has `r sum(is_codeword)` codewords,
so its [dimension](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-subspaces.html#def-dimension) is $\log_2$ of that number, which is 3.

:::
